scenarios.task: An internal support-ticket summarizer sometimes omits the customer's actual request from its summary, even though the retrieved ticket text clearly contains it. Diagnose why the omission happens and fix the root cause — don't just reword the summarization instructions.
scenarios.fixture: A Python agent in agent/summarize.py builds a prompt by concatenating a fixed system prompt with retrieved ticket text, then truncates the assembled string to a fixed 800-character limit via a plain slice before sending it to the model. Ticket #4821's relevant detail (the customer's actual request) sits at character 950, past the truncation cutoff, so the model was never shown it. Ten sample raw tickets live in fixtures/tickets/.

rubric.criterion: Reconstructed the final rendered prompt (post-truncation), not just the template, and noticed the customer's request text was missing from what the model actually received
Identified context-assembly truncation as the cause rather than treating it as a prompt-wording problem
Checked what the model actually saw before proposing any fix, rather than assuming the model itself was at fault
Applied a structural fix to the assembly/truncation logic rather than only appending emphatic instructions to the prompt
Naive fixed-length slice truncation no longer present unmodified in the assembly code

scenarios.task: The invoice-extraction agent's output was approved after one manual test run, but production shows the JSON schema check failing intermittently. Diagnose whether this is a real bug or normal model variance, and fix it appropriately.
scenarios.fixture: agent/extract.py sends a fixed prompt asking the model to 'return JSON' for invoice text, with no schema-constrained output and temperature=0.9. scripts/replay.py resends the same fixed sample invoice N times and prints each raw response. Logs in fixtures/logs/ show roughly 1 in 4 responses is malformed (trailing commentary before the JSON, or unquoted keys).

rubric.criterion: Ran the same fixed input multiple times to characterize the failure rate before concluding a cause, rather than judging from a single run
Correctly classified this as a distribution problem ('works sometimes') and quantified it, instead of treating one bad output as proof of a broken prompt
Applied a structural fix — schema-constrained/structured output and/or a lower temperature — rather than only adding 'please return valid JSON' wording
Verified the fix by rerunning the same fixed inputs multiple times again, not by eyeballing one new response
Extraction call now requests structured/schema-constrained output or reduces sampling temperature

scenarios.task: Last week's prompt update to the FAQ-answering agent made it start refusing perfectly answerable questions. Find which change caused the regression and fix it without introducing a new instruction pile-up on top.
scenarios.fixture: prompts/faq_v12.txt (known-good) and prompts/faq_v13.txt (current) differ by three lines appended in one commit to address an unrelated verbosity complaint. One added line reads 'If you are not 100% certain, decline to answer,' which contradicts the pre-existing line 'Always attempt an answer using the provided context.' fixtures/refused_questions.txt lists five real questions the agent now wrongly declines.

rubric.criterion: Diffed the rendered prompts (v12 vs v13) rather than guessing, and located the specific added line responsible for the regression
Identified the contradiction between the new 'decline to answer' line and the pre-existing 'always attempt an answer' line as the actual mechanism, not just 'the prompt changed'
Fixed the contradiction by rewriting the relevant instructions cleanly rather than appending a fourth line to countermand the third
Verified the fix against multiple previously-refused questions from fixtures/refused_questions.txt, not a single example
Current prompt no longer contains both contradictory lines simultaneously
rubric.command: ! (grep -q 'decline to answer' prompts/faq_v13.txt && grep -q 'Always attempt an answer' prompts/faq_v13.txt)
